reasons.text: From the David Raya (£6.3m) latest to yet another match without any minutes for William Saliba (£5.9m), here are our Scout Notes from the midweek UEFA Champions League game at the Emirates.
In this piece I will look briefly at how to manage the fixture congestion, David Raya’s injury and all the sucky premiums.
Raya could be back by next FPL gameweek or out for months based on how much we trust Arteta.
Kepa Arrizabalaga deputised at the Emirates Stadium, with Arteta offering his backing to the goalkeeper should Raya remain unavailable this weekend.

What is the latest on David Raya's injury? © Iconsport / PA Images Raya left the pitch in significant pain during Arsenal's 2-2 draw with the Magpies on Saturday night, prompting fears that he could face a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

Arteta confirms Raya needs no surgery: Arsenal's keeper Arsenal keep Raya with seven clean sheets in 11 games Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya does not need surgery on the shoulder injury he suffered, Mikel Arteta has confirmed, and the problem is 'not too serious'.
Raya has kept seven clean sheets in 11 league games, and Arsenal have conceded only seven goals all season in the division.
Raya exited Saturday’s 2–2 draw with Newcastle United holding his arm after suffering an injury in what initially did not seem to be significant contact with Magpies striker William Osula.
Arsenal team news David Raya will miss out for Arsenal with a shoulder injury; Kepa Arrizabalaga will take his place.
Add in Arsenal without goalkeeper David Raya and Dortmund may have the opportunity to make life uncomfortable for the hosts.
Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has revealed that David Raya won’t be fit to face Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League but his injury “doesn’t look too serious”.
The Arsenal boss also revealed that Raya would undergo an MRI scan on Sunday to assess the seriousness of the issue, and on the same day, he was photographed with his arm in a sling in London.
Raya played a key role as Arsenal ended a 22-year wait for a Premier League title last season and had started this campaign with seven clean sheets in 10 matches before the match in Newcastle.
Raya's injury came on the day Arsenal welcomed back William Saliba to the matchday squad.
Saka will not be available till mid-to-late December , while Zubimendi was ruled out for “a few weeks” just last Friday The third absentee, again as expected, was David Raya .
Raya will miss Tuesday’s clash with Borussia Dortmund but, encouragingly, Arteta said the Spaniard’s issue “doesn’t look too serious”.
As you’ll no doubt know by now, David Raya (£6.3m), Fantasy Premier League’s (FPL) top-scoring and most-owned goalkeeper, picked up a shoulder injury against Newcastle United on Saturday.

Joe Prince-Wright Joe Prince-Wright Published November 22, 2026 05:22 AM Add on Google Facebook Twitter Email Add on Google Arsenal fans will be sweating on the latest David Raya injury news, with their star goalkeeper coming off against Newcastle on Saturday and it didn’t look great.

Even though they recovered after Raya’s injury and fought back to make it 2-2 and grab a point Aside from the result Arteta will be very concerned about Raya, who was subbed off looking in real pain, with Kepa Arrizabalaga coming on in his place.

Arteta confirms MRI scan for injured Raya © Iconsport / Action Plus Speaking after the full-time whistle, Arteta viewed the result as two points dropped rather than one gained and admitted his goalkeeper's setback is a genuine concern.
David Raya (£6.3m) was in the wars on Tyneside, needing treatment on a couple of occasions.
Raya looked in some pain and seemed to be struggling with his collarbone or shoulder .
Raya ‌left the field holding his left arm ‌in the 70th minute and was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga "Unfortunately, ‌he had to come off, which is never ‌good news.

Malick Thiaw prodded in from close range following a corner as the Magpies deservedly turned the scoreline around 13 minutes later, with Arsenal’s concerns compounded when Kai Havertz headed against his own crossbar shortly after David Raya was forced off with an apparent injury to the goalkeeper’s left arm.

Second-placed Brighton & Hove Albion can cut the gap to three points by winning at Hull City on Sunday, while the injury to Raya, who was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga, will be of considerable concern to Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta.

David Raya © Iconsport / Maynard Manyowa/News Images/Sipa USA Status: Out Type of injury: Shoulder Possible return date: Unknown After a seemingly innocuous coming together with Newcastle's Will Osula on Saturday, Arsenal number one David Raya was worryingly taken off in some pain with a shoulder injury.
Raya is the number one goalkeeper for Arsenal and is one of the best in the world.
As expected, Raya started in goal for Arsenal in their Premier League game against Newcastle United away from home at St. James’ Park on Saturday evening.

If you still have a Wildcard in hand or are considering a transfer at the back and you don’t want to splurge £6.3m on David Raya , I’ve come up with three goalkeeper pairings that are worthy of consideration.
Another advantage is that Kinsky being £4.4m makes this pair cost a lot less than David Raya (£6.2m) and a £4.0m bench option.
On Tuesday morning, Sky Sports , citing The Athletic , reported in its live coverage that goalkeeper Raya, 31, had also agreed a new long-term contract.

The Spaniard joined from Brentford in 2023, initially on loan, to the confusion of some fans who felt that then-keeper Aaron Ramsdale didn't need replacing, but Raya won over doubters with excellent reflex saves, superb cross-claiming and world-class distribution.

reasons.text: From the David Raya (£6.3m) latest to yet another match without any minutes for William Saliba (£5.9m), here are our Scout Notes from the midweek UEFA Champions League game at the Emirates.
In this piece I will look briefly at how to manage the fixture congestion, David Raya’s injury and all the sucky premiums.
Raya could be back by next FPL gameweek or out for months based on how much we trust Arteta.
Kepa Arrizabalaga deputised at the Emirates Stadium, with Arteta offering his backing to the goalkeeper should Raya remain unavailable this weekend.

What is the latest on David Raya's injury? © Iconsport / PA Images Raya left the pitch in significant pain during Arsenal's 2-2 draw with the Magpies on Saturday night, prompting fears that he could face a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

Arteta confirms Raya needs no surgery: Arsenal's keeper Arsenal keep Raya with seven clean sheets in 11 games Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya does not need surgery on the shoulder injury he suffered, Mikel Arteta has confirmed, and the problem is 'not too serious'.
Raya has kept seven clean sheets in 11 league games, and Arsenal have conceded only seven goals all season in the division.
Raya exited Saturday’s 2–2 draw with Newcastle United holding his arm after suffering an injury in what initially did not seem to be significant contact with Magpies striker William Osula.
Arsenal team news David Raya will miss out for Arsenal with a shoulder injury; Kepa Arrizabalaga will take his place.
Add in Arsenal without goalkeeper David Raya and Dortmund may have the opportunity to make life uncomfortable for the hosts.
Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has revealed that David Raya won’t be fit to face Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League but his injury “doesn’t look too serious”.
The Arsenal boss also revealed that Raya would undergo an MRI scan on Sunday to assess the seriousness of the issue, and on the same day, he was photographed with his arm in a sling in London.
Raya played a key role as Arsenal ended a 22-year wait for a Premier League title last season and had started this campaign with seven clean sheets in 10 matches before the match in Newcastle.
Raya's injury came on the day Arsenal welcomed back William Saliba to the matchday squad.
Saka will not be available till mid-to-late December , while Zubimendi was ruled out for “a few weeks” just last Friday The third absentee, again as expected, was David Raya .
Raya will miss Tuesday’s clash with Borussia Dortmund but, encouragingly, Arteta said the Spaniard’s issue “doesn’t look too serious”.
As you’ll no doubt know by now, David Raya (£6.3m), Fantasy Premier League’s (FPL) top-scoring and most-owned goalkeeper, picked up a shoulder injury against Newcastle United on Saturday.

Joe Prince-Wright Joe Prince-Wright Published November 22, 2026 05:22 AM Add on Google Facebook Twitter Email Add on Google Arsenal fans will be sweating on the latest David Raya injury news, with their star goalkeeper coming off against Newcastle on Saturday and it didn’t look great.

Even though they recovered after Raya’s injury and fought back to make it 2-2 and grab a point Aside from the result Arteta will be very concerned about Raya, who was subbed off looking in real pain, with Kepa Arrizabalaga coming on in his place.

Arteta confirms MRI scan for injured Raya © Iconsport / Action Plus Speaking after the full-time whistle, Arteta viewed the result as two points dropped rather than one gained and admitted his goalkeeper's setback is a genuine concern.
David Raya (£6.3m) was in the wars on Tyneside, needing treatment on a couple of occasions.

It was De Cuyper’s goal that proved the catalyst for his side’s comeback.

He had two goal involvements in 18 minutes and a hand in a third in the opening 4-0 win against Aston Villa Matty Cash spent the whole first half caught between two jobs: following De Cuyper inside or holding his line.
It’s been a whirlwind ‘out of position’ ride with De Cuyper this season, and there’s little sign of a slowdown.
De Cuyper’s not an issue for now, then, even if Luka Vuskovic (£5.2m) will likely end up being the long, long-term best pick at the back.

Having provided an assist in the Red Devils’ victory over Turkey last Thursday, De Cuyper followed that up with a goal in Belgium’s riotous 4-1 win against Italy on Sunday.
It was De Cuyper’s goal that proved the catalyst for his side’s comeback.

He had two goal involvements in 18 minutes and a hand in a third in the opening 4-0 win against Aston Villa Matty Cash spent the whole first half caught between two jobs: following De Cuyper inside or holding his line.
It’s been a whirlwind ‘out of position’ ride with De Cuyper this season, and there’s little sign of a slowdown.
De Cuyper’s not an issue for now, then, even if Luka Vuskovic (£5.2m) will likely end up being the long, long-term best pick at the back.
